findings.title: Command injection vulnerability in get_cli_string
findings.description: The function `get_cli_string` builds a shell command string intended to be executed in shell contexts (such as Fabric tasks). It performs rudimentary quoting only if a space exists in `value`, but does not escape shell metacharacters (e.g. `;`, `&`, `|`, `` ` ``, `$()`, or embedded quotes) in `value`, `key`, or `path`. Passing user-controlled inputs into this function leads to command injection.
findings.suggestion: Use `shlex.quote` from the standard library to sanitize all parameters (`path`, `key`, `value`, `quote`) before concatenating them into the shell command string.

findings.title: Assert statement used for frame traversal control flow in find_dotenv
findings.description: In `find_dotenv`, the loop navigating caller frames uses `assert frame.f_back is not None`. When Python is executed with optimization flags (`python -O`), assertions are stripped, which can cause `frame = frame.f_back` to set `frame = None` and raise `AttributeError` on the subsequent iteration. In non-optimized mode, reaching the top of the call stack (e.g. in dynamically executed code or certain execution environments) raises an unhandled `AssertionError` instead of falling back gracefully.
findings.suggestion: Replace `assert frame.f_back is not None` with an explicit check: `if frame.f_back is None: break` and fall back to `os.getcwd()` or raise an `IOError`.

findings.title: test_list checks built-in format function instead of output_format argument
findings.description: In `test_list`, the condition `if format is not None:` references the Python built-in `format` function rather than the test argument `output_format`. Because `format` is always a function object (never `None`), the condition is always true. When testing the default case where `output_format` is `None`, `args.extend(["--format", None])` is executed, preventing the test from exercising the command when `--format` is omitted.
findings.suggestion: Change `if format is not None:` to `if output_format is not None:`.

findings.title: test_list_no_file and test_set_non_existent_file pass due to unhandled TypeError in Click context
findings.description: `test_list_no_file` and `test_set_non_existent_file` invoke subcommands `dotenv.cli.list_values` and `dotenv.cli.set_value` directly via `cli.invoke` without the parent Click group context. `ctx.obj` is therefore `None`, causing `ctx.obj["FILE"]` to crash with `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable`. Click catches the unhandled exception and exits with code 1, which masks the fact that the tests are not actually testing file existence logic.
findings.suggestion: Invoke through the main CLI group `dotenv_cli` (e.g. `cli.invoke(dotenv_cli, ["list"])` or `cli.invoke(dotenv_cli, ["set", "a", "b"])`) or explicitly pass `obj={"FILE": None, ...}` in `cli.invoke`.

findings.title: test_run_without_cmd fails at file check rather than testing missing commandline branch
findings.description: In `test_run_without_cmd`, `run_dotenv(["run"], cwd=tmp_path)` is executed in an empty `tmp_path` without a `.env` file. It fails with exit code 2 at the earlier `if not os.path.isfile(file):` check rather than testing the `if not commandline:` branch in `run()` (which outputs 'No command given.' and exits with 1). As a result, the missing command validation path is untested.
findings.suggestion: Create a dummy `.env` file in `tmp_path` prior to calling `run_dotenv(["run"], cwd=tmp_path)` and assert `exit_code == 1` and `stdout == 'No command given.\n'`.

findings.title: Duplicate test case for multiline double-quoted values in test_parse_stream
findings.description:
The test case `('a="b
c"', [Binding(key="a", value="b
c", original=Original(string='a="b
c"', line=1), error=False)])` appears identically at lines 211-222 and again at lines 235-246.
findings.suggestion: Remove the redundant parametrized test case.

findings.title: dotenv run rejects FIFOs due to os.path.isfile check
findings.description: python-dotenv 1.2.0+ supports reading `.env` configurations from FIFOs (named pipes) via `_is_file_or_fifo`. However, the CLI command `run` checks `if not os.path.isfile(file):`. On Unix systems, FIFOs return `False` for `os.path.isfile`, causing `dotenv -f <fifo> run ...` to fail with a `BadParameter` error despite FIFO support being an advertised feature.
findings.suggestion: Import `_is_file_or_fifo` from `dotenv.main` and use `if not _is_file_or_fifo(file):` instead of `os.path.isfile(file)`.

findings.title: dotenv get fails with exit code 1 for empty string values
findings.description: In `get`, the check `if stored_value:` evaluates to `False` when a key exists in `.env` with an empty string value (e.g. `EMPTY=`). The command exits with error code 1 without printing output, incorrectly treating an empty value as a missing key.
findings.suggestion: Change `if stored_value:` to `if stored_value is not None:`.

findings.title: Unused quote_mode parameter and inconsistent parameter ordering in unset_key
findings.description: `unset_key` accepts `quote_mode: str = "always"`, but the parameter is never used anywhere in the function. In contrast, `get_key` takes `(dotenv_path, key_to_get, encoding="utf-8")` where the 3rd parameter is `encoding`. In `unset_key`, the 3rd parameter is `quote_mode`, causing positional calls like `unset_key(path, key, "utf-8")` to silently misassign encoding to `quote_mode`.
findings.suggestion: Deprecate and remove `quote_mode` from `unset_key` and align the parameter signature with `get_key` (`encoding` as 3rd parameter).

findings.title: Inconsistent default values between DotEnv.__init__ and public loader functions
findings.description: `DotEnv.__init__` defaults `override=True` and `encoding=None`, whereas public APIs `load_dotenv` and `dotenv_values` default `override=False` and `encoding="utf-8"`. Instantiating `DotEnv` directly produces different behavior from calling `load_dotenv` with defaults.
findings.suggestion: Align default parameter values in `DotEnv.__init__` (`override: bool = False`, `encoding: Optional[str] = "utf-8"`) with `load_dotenv`.

findings.title: Invalid CLI commands in contributing guide
findings.description: The commands `uv ruff check .`, `uv format .`, and `uv run precommit install` in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (and `docs/contributing.md`) are invalid. `uv` does not have `ruff` or `format` subcommands (they require `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format .`), and the pre-commit binary is `pre-commit`, not `precommit`.
findings.suggestion: Update the documentation to use valid commands: `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format .`, and `uv run pre-commit install`.

findings.title: Markdown header prefix prevents mkdocstrings plugin from generating API reference
findings.description: `docs/reference.md` contains `# ::: dotenv`. The leading `#` renders this line as a plain Markdown title rather than the mkdocstrings directive `::: dotenv`. As a result, no API reference documentation is generated for the package.
findings.suggestion: Remove the `# ` prefix so line 1 reads `::: dotenv`.

findings.title: Empty markdown link for mkdocs in contributing docs
findings.description: In `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/contributing.md`, the link `[mkdocs]()` has an empty URL destination.
findings.suggestion: Provide the documentation URL, e.g. `[mkdocs](https://www.mkdocs.org/)`.

findings.title: Typographical error in changelog breaking changes section
findings.description: In `CHANGELOG.md` (and `docs/changelog.md`) under version [1.2.2], the line reads: 'Is the file needed to be created or wasn't a regular file, mode 0o600 is used.' The word 'Is' is a typo for 'If'.
findings.suggestion: Change 'Is the file needed to be created' to 'If the file needed to be created'.

findings.title: py.typed package data declared but file is missing from repository
findings.description: `pyproject.toml` declares `package-data = {dotenv = ["py.typed"]} `, but no `py.typed` file exists inside `src/dotenv/`. Downstream type checkers (e.g. Mypy, Pyright) relying on PEP 561 will fail to recognize `python-dotenv` as a typed library.
findings.suggestion: Create an empty `src/dotenv/py.typed` file so type information is distributed in wheels and source distributions.

findings.title: Documentation files duplicated across root and docs/ directory
findings.description: `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` are duplicated verbatim as `docs/index.md`, `docs/changelog.md`, and `docs/contributing.md`. This duplication leads to content drift when changes are applied to one set of files but not the other.
findings.suggestion: Use MkDocs plugins (such as `mkdocs-include-markdown-plugin` or symlinks) to include root Markdown files into the documentation site rather than maintaining duplicate copies.

findings.title: Deprecated bumpversion package in requirements.txt
findings.description: `requirements.txt` specifies `bumpversion`, which has been abandoned and unmaintained since ~2015. It lacks compatibility with modern Python packaging and pyproject.toml configuration.
findings.suggestion: Replace `bumpversion` with `bump-my-version` or `bump2version`.

findings.title: Unused mkdocs-include-markdown-plugin dependency
findings.description: `mkdocs-include-markdown-plugin` is listed in `requirements-docs.txt`, but it is not listed in `plugins` within `mkdocs.yml` nor used anywhere in documentation source files.
findings.suggestion: Either configure `mkdocs-include-markdown-plugin` in `mkdocs.yml` to eliminate duplicated doc files, or remove it from `requirements-docs.txt`.

findings.title: Quadratic dictionary copying in resolve_variables
findings.description: In `resolve_variables`, `env = {}` is initialized and `os.environ` plus all previously resolved keys (`new_values`) are copied into it for every single variable in `values`. For a file with N variables and M environment variables, this results in O(N * M + N^2) dictionary insertions and allocations.
findings.suggestion: Maintain a persistent dictionary or use `collections.ChainMap` rather than recreating and copying the entire environment dict on every iteration.

findings.title: Cached dict bypassed for empty .env files in DotEnv.dict
findings.description: `DotEnv.dict()` checks `if self._dict:` before parsing. If the `.env` file is empty, `self._dict` is `{}` (an empty dict), which evaluates to `False`. Subsequent calls to `dict()` on the same instance re-open the file and re-parse from scratch on every call instead of returning the cached dictionary.
findings.suggestion: Change `if self._dict:` to `if self._dict is not None:`.
